context.title: Saul Meets the Risen Jesus
context.summary: Saul, heading to Damascus to arrest believers, is stopped by a light and the voice of Jesus. Blinded, he is healed and baptized through Ananias, preaches boldly, and escapes plots. Peter heals Aeneas and raises Tabitha.
context.background: Damascus, well over a hundred miles north of Jerusalem, had a large Jewish community. The high priest's letters asked its synagogues to help arrest any 'of this way' (v. 2), an early name for the movement. Paul tells this story twice more (chapters 22 and 26).

customs.note: Damascus' main east-west street, a Roman colonnaded avenue whose line can still be traced in the old city.
Houses were sometimes built into city walls, and a large basket on a rope could lower a man through a window (2 Corinthians 11:33).

watchFor: 'Why persecutest thou me?' Jesus identifies with his people (v. 4).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Paul
people.summary: Saul was born about the same time as our Lord. His circumcision-name was Saul, and probably the name Paul was also given to him in infancy “for use in the Gentile world,” as “Saul” would be his Hebrew home-name.

people.name: Ananias
people.summary: A Christian at Damascus (Acts 9:10). He became Paul’s instructor; but when or by what means he himself became a Christian we have no information.

people.name: Judas
people.summary: A Jew of Damascus (Acts 9:11), to whose house Ananias was sent.

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Barnabas
people.summary: Son of consolation, the surname of Joses, a Levite (Acts 4:36). His name stands first on the list of prophets and teachers of the church at Antioch (13:1).

people.name: Simon
people.summary: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture.

people.name: Dorcas
people.summary: (in Greek called Dorcas), gazelle, a disciple at Joppa. She was distinguished for her alms-deeds and good works. Peter, who was sent for from Lydda on the occasion of her death, prayed over the dead body, and said, “Tabitha, arise.”

people.name: Simon
people.summary: A Christian at Joppa, a tanner by trade, with whom Peter on one occasion lodged (Acts 9:43).

places.name: Damascus
places.summary: Activity, the most ancient of Oriental cities; the capital of Syria (Isa. 7:8; 17:3); situated about 133 miles to the north of Jerusalem.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Straight Gate
places.summary: The street called “Straight” at Damascus (Acts 9:11) is “a long broad street, running from east to west, about a mile in length, and forming the principal thoroughfare in the city.”

places.name: Tarsus
places.summary: The chief city of Cilicia. It was distinguished for its wealth and for its schools of learning, in which it rivalled, nay, excelled even Athens and Alexandria, and hence was spoken of as “no mean city.”

places.name: Caesarea
places.summary: (Palestinae), a city on the shore of the Mediterranean, on the great road from Tyre to Egypt, about 70 miles northwest of Jerusalem, at the northern extremity of the plain of Sharon.

places.name: Galilee
places.summary: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali. Hiram was dissatisfied with the gift, and called it “the land of Cabul”.

places.name: Judea
places.summary: After the Captivity this name was applied to the whole of the country west of the Jordan (Hag. 1:1, 14; 2:2).

places.name: Samaria
places.summary: A watch-mountain or a watch-tower. In the heart of the mountains of Israel, a few miles north-west of Shechem, stands the “hill of Shomeron,” a solitary mountain, a great “mamelon.”

places.name: Lydda
places.summary: A town in the tribe of Ephraim, mentioned only in the New Testament (Acts 9:32, 35, 38) as the scene of Peter’s miracle in healing the paralytic AEneas.

places.name: Saron
places.summary: A plain, a level tract extending from the Mediterranean to the hill country to the west of Jerusalem, about 30 miles long and from 8 to 15 miles broad, celebrated for its beauty and fertility (1 Chr. 27:29; Isa. 33:9; 35:2; 65:10).

places.name: Joppa
places.summary: Beauty, a town in the portion of Dan (Josh. 19:46; A.V., “Japho”), on a sandy promontory between Caesarea and Gaza, and at a distance of 30 miles north-west from Jerusalem.

events.title: Saul is converted
events.summary: Passage: Acts 9:1–19. People: Holy Spirit, Ananias, Paul. Place: Straight Gate, Damascus.

events.title: Saul proclaims Jesus
events.summary: Passage: Acts 9:20–31. People: Holy Spirit, Barnabas, Paul. Place: Tarsus, Caesarea, Damascus, Jerusalem.

events.title: Peter heals Aeneas and Dorcas
events.summary: Passage: Acts 9:32–43. People: Simon, Dorcas, Aeneas. Place: Joppa, Saron, Lydda.
